name.text: Draw the tangent at a marked point (INNODEMS)

questiontext.text:
The blue curve is the graph of a function \(f\). The red point \(P\) is marked on the curve.

Drag the two blue points \(A\) and \(B\) so that the green line is the tangent to the curve at \(P\). The tangent just touches the curve at \(P\) and runs in the same direction as the curve there.

[[jsxgraph input-ref-ans1="ref_A" input-ref-ans2="ref_B" width='480px' height='480px']] var aa = {#float(aa)#}, pp = {#float(pp)#}, hh = {#float(hh)#}, kk = {#float(kk)#}; var x0 = {#float(x0)#}, y0 = {#float(y0)#}, A = {#float(A)#}; var Aix = {#float(Aix)#}, Aiy = {#float(Aiy)#}; var Bix = {#float(Bix)#}, Biy = {#float(Biy)#}; function f(x){ var t = x - hh; return aa*t*t*t + pp*t + kk; } // Fixed square window [-A,A]^2 on a square board => genuine equal x/y scale. var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-A, A, A, -A], keepAspectRatio: true, axis: true, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: true, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: true} }); // The curve, drawn across the full width (exits top/bottom where steep - // clipped naturally). No formula label: the student reads the graph. board.create('functiongraph', [f, -A, A], {strokeColor: '#0055bb', strokeWidth: 2.5, name: '', highlight: false}); // Marked tangent point P (fixed). board.create('point', [x0, y0], {name: 'P', size: 2, fixed: true, fillColor: '#d32f2f', strokeColor: '#d32f2f', label: {offset: [8, -18], color: '#d32f2f', fontSize: 15}}); // Two draggable points that define the student's line. They start as a secant // to the LEFT of P (clearly not the tangent), so doing nothing scores zero. var A = board.create('point', [Aix, Aiy], {name: 'A', size: 2, strokeColor: '#1565c0', fillColor: '#1565c0', snapToGrid: false, label: {offset: [-16, 8], color: '#1565c0', fontSize: 14}}); var B = board.create('point', [Bix, Biy], {name: 'B', size: 2, strokeColor: '#1565c0', fillColor: '#1565c0', snapToGrid: false, label: {offset: [10, 8], color: '#1565c0', fontSize: 14}}); // The student's line through A and B. board.create('line', [A, B], {strokeColor: '#2e7d32', strokeWidth: 2.5, straightFirst: true, straightLast: true, highlight: false}); // Live readout: the equation of the student's current line (their "formula"). board.create('text', [-A + 0.3, A - 0.4, function () { var ax = A.X(), ay = A.Y(), bx = B.X(), by = B.Y(); var eq; if (Math.abs(bx - ax) < 1e-6) { eq = 'x = ' + ax.toFixed(2) + ' (vertical)'; } else { var m = (by - ay) / (bx - ax); var c = ay - m * ax; var cs = (c >= 0) ? ('+ ' + c.toFixed(2)) : ('− ' + Math.abs(c).toFixed(2)); eq = 'y = ' + m.toFixed(2) + 'x ' + cs; } return '
' + 'Your line:  ' + eq + '
'; }], {useHTML: true, anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'top', fixed: true}); stack_jxg.bind_point(ref_A, A); stack_jxg.bind_point(ref_B, B); [[/jsxgraph]]

generalfeedback.text:
The tangent at \(P\) is the straight line that just touches the curve there and runs in the same direction as the curve — its slope is the value of the derivative \(f'\) at that point.

Here the tangent at \(P = ({@x0@},\, {@y0@})\) has slope \(f'({@x0@}) = {@m0@}\), so its equation is \[ y = {@y0@} + ({@m0@})\,\bigl(x - ({@x0@})\bigr) = {@tanline@}. \]

(The hidden curve is \(f(x) = {@fpoly@}\); the differentiation rules in the later sections will confirm \(f'({@x0@}) = {@m0@}\).)

[[jsxgraph width='380px' height='380px']] var aa = {#float(aa)#}, pp = {#float(pp)#}, hh = {#float(hh)#}, kk = {#float(kk)#}; var x0 = {#float(x0)#}, y0 = {#float(y0)#}, m0 = {#float(m0)#}, A = {#float(A)#}; function f(x){ var t = x - hh; return aa*t*t*t + pp*t + kk; } function tang(x){ return y0 + m0*(x - x0); } var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-A, A, A, -A], keepAspectRatio: true, axis: true, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false} }); board.create('functiongraph', [f, -A, A], {strokeColor: '#0055bb', strokeWidth: 2.5, name: '', highlight: false}); board.create('functiongraph', [tang, -A, A], {strokeColor: '#2e7d32', strokeWidth: 2, dash: 0, name: '', highlight: false}); board.create('point', [x0, y0], {name: 'P', size: 4, fixed: true, fillColor: '#d32f2f', strokeColor: '#d32f2f', label: {offset: [8, -18], color: '#d32f2f', fontSize: 14}}); [[/jsxgraph]]

truefeedback.text: Your two points share (almost) the same \(x\)-value, so the line is nearly vertical. The tangent here isn't vertical — give \(A\) and \(B\) clearly different \(x\)-coordinates.
Correct — your line just touches the curve at \(P\) and matches its steepness there. That slope is the derivative \(f'\) at \(P\).

falsefeedback.text: Your line has about the right steepness, but it doesn't pass through \(P\). Slide it (keeping its slope) until it touches the curve exactly at the marked point.

truefeedback.text: Your line is perpendicular to the curve at \(P\) — that's the normal, not the tangent (the normal comes up in a later section). The tangent runs along the curve's direction at \(P\), not across it.

node.description: Passes through P but wrong slope (a secant/chord)?

truefeedback.text: Your line passes through \(P\) but crosses the curve rather than just touching it — it's a chord joining \(P\) to another point on the curve. A tangent only touches at \(P\); rotate your line so it matches the curve's steepness right at \(P\).

falsefeedback.text: Not the tangent yet. It should just touch the curve at \(P\) and run in the same direction as the curve there. Put one point on \(P\), then rotate the other until the line hugs the curve at \(P\) — the readout shows your line's equation to help.

qtest.description: Correct tangent: two points on the line through P with slope f'(x0).
Secant/chord through P (right position, wrong slope).
Right slope but misses P (tangent shifted up).
Near-vertical line (same x for both points).
